Velvet Meadow brings a new psychedelic pop single "Ive Come To Realize" which is track 3 off his upcoming new psych pop/rock album coming 2024 "Never Want To Leave My Head". During the year of 2023 Kris Heironimus was struggling for inspiration for his new album. He spent two months just listening to his favorite artists, and experimenting with self taught production tricks. After blasting the Beatles Magical Mystery Tour,  MGMTs Congratulations, PONDS The Weather, and many other amazing psych artists he took a new direction with his music Focusing heavily on sonic textures as well as pop lyrics and melodies. "Ive Come To Realize" pushes the boundaries of mainstream pop norms as well as progressing the indie soundscape deeper into the unknown. Sit back and sink into the couch because this one will be a ride! 

Press:

Synth shimmers and a deeply grooving bass line traverse into a hazy vocal, singing “she’s got me in her heart-shaped box,” with a soaring intrigue. The vocals ascend alongside buzzing synth insertions just prior to the one-minute mark, taking this already-riveting psychedelic soundscape to the next level. “Let me show you, sweetheart, just give me one try,” the vocals plead further, emitting a sense of yearning amidst the steady production and title-touting punctuation. “Ive Come To Realize” is a stellar psych-forward success from Velvet Meadow. - Mike Mineo // Obscure Sound

This Mixtape Edition is a raw intimate glimpse at the emotional journey that shaped "seeing red feeling blue". 

The success of my Love Letters Music NFT collection was a game-changer, propelling me from the uncertainty of independent artistry to the unimaginable — touring with Snow Patrol and Robbie Williams. In a music world dominated by major labels, web3 gave me a chance to break through barriers, but it also brought a whirlwind of highs and lows. This EP was born from that rollercoaster, capturing both the euphoric thrill of success and the crushing lows of hitting rock bottom, wrestling with doubt and uncertainty.

Each track on this mixtape tells a part of that story—from the resilience in “Fight Another Day” to the introspection of “Sleep On It.” This digital mixtape is a rare, limited-edition piece, created for those who’ve been an integral part of this journey and want to hold onto a piece of its legacy.

First access is reserved for my Love Letters and Stamps Music NFT holders.

The song "Lover Lie Away" by KarimReslan explores themes of deception, attraction, and the desire for honesty in a romantic relationship.

The repeated phrase "Lover lie away" suggests that the person singing or the protagonist of the song is asking their lover to refrain from lying. This could be a plea for transparency and sincerity in the relationship.

The lyrics express a desire for the lover to stay and not hide, indicating a longing for their presence and emotional connection. It portrays a yearning for a genuine and open connection with the partner.

The mention of the lover being like jewelry at a party and dancing suggests a sense of physical attraction and allure. However, the protagonist feels deceived by this initial attraction, as indicated by the line "She wanted what I be experiencing daily." This may imply that the lover was more interested in the persona or lifestyle of the protagonist rather than a genuine connection.

The lyrics also mention the protagonist's hesitation to engage with the lover, describing the encounter as somewhat tedious and uninteresting. This could be an acknowledgment of the lack of depth or emotional fulfillment in the relationship.

Towards the end of the song, there is a reference to the lover disclosing that she is a dancer. The subsequent lines indicate a dissatisfaction with this revelation and a desire to end things, suggesting a realization that their connection was not founded on genuine emotional compatibility. This part of the lyrics may allude to the idea that the relationship was transactional or based on superficial qualities, leading to a feeling of dissatisfaction and the decision to break things off.

Overall, "Lover Lie Away" expresses a longing for honesty, authenticity, and emotional connection in a romantic relationship while highlighting the consequences of superficial attraction and a lack of genuine compatibility.

“#E788A0” by WarBaby of Outside The Wire Productions is a true testament to raw human expression—a one-of-a-kind digital asset that can never be replicated by AI or machines. 

This NFT captures the organic, hand-crafted artistry that emerged from the depths of personal experience. Each sound and layer was crafted “from scratch,” reflecting the intense emotions born from WarBaby’s time in the U.S. Army, especially during high-stakes moments in the Middle East. Music became a mental escape from the chaos around him, transforming adrenaline and inner conflict into powerful soundscapes. 

The audio was professionally and delicately designed, using specific frequencies chosen to heal through sound, frequency, and vibration. This timeless piece of artwork is not only unique; it stands as a tribute to the resilience and authenticity that only human touch can create.

Mizter Bonezz - Lifetime Trip: A Journey Through Sound and Experience

Overview:
“Lifetime Trip” is a captivating track by Mizter Bonezz, a producer known for his intricate and emotional compositions. This song captures the essence of a profound journey, weaving together elements of psytrance, dubstep, and electronic music to create an immersive auditory experience.

Musical Composition:
The track is a masterful blend of pulsating basslines, hypnotic rhythms, and ethereal melodies. It opens with a serene yet mysterious intro, gradually building into a powerful, driving beat that propels listeners into a state of euphoria. The tempo transitions are a defining feature, starting at 160 BPM, escalating to a peak of 200 BPM, and then settling back to 150 BPM. These shifts in tempo create a dynamic and engaging listening experience, reflecting the unpredictable nature of life’s journey. The inclusion of dubstep elements adds a gritty, energetic layer, with wobbly basslines and syncopated rhythms that enhance the track’s intensity.

Emotional Journey:
“Lifetime Trip” is more than just a song; it’s an emotional voyage. The track’s progression mirrors the ups and downs of a lifetime, taking listeners through moments of introspection, exhilaration, and transcendence. The dynamic shifts in tempo and intensity, combined with the heavy drops and melodic interludes typical of dubstep, enhance the emotional depth, making the experience deeply personal and relatable.

Production Quality:
Mizter Bonezz showcases his exceptional production skills in “Lifetime Trip.” Every element is meticulously crafted, with a clear focus on creating a pristine soundscape. The use of spatial effects and stereo imaging enhances the immersive quality of the track, making it a standout piece in his discography. The precise control over the varying BPMs and the seamless integration of psytrance and dubstep elements demonstrate his technical prowess and creativity.

Impact on Listeners:
Fans of Mizter Bonezz have praised “Lifetime Trip” for its ability to transport them to another realm. The track has become a favorite in live performances and DJ sets, resonating with audiences for its emotional depth and high-energy delivery. The fluctuating BPMs and the infusion of dubstep elements keep listeners engaged and excited, ensuring that every moment is captivating.

Who is Mizter Bonezz?

Background:
Mizter Bonezz, born Daniel Amaya on August 13, 1992, is a dynamic and resilient DJ and music producer hailing from Sylmar, California. Known for his versatility and emotional depth in music, Mizter Bonezz has carved out a unique niche in the electronic music scene, blending psytrance, dubstep, and other electronic subgenres to create immersive auditory experiences.

Early Life and Challenges:
Mizter Bonezz’s journey is marked by overcoming significant challenges. He has endured over 300 fractures and undergone more than 18 surgeries due to Osteogenesis Imperfecta, a condition that has shaped much of his life and music. In 2015, he experienced two hypoxic respiratory failures, leading to a life-changing tracheostomy surgery. This surgery left him unable to speak for almost a year and dependent on a feeding tube. Despite these hardships, he has channeled his experiences into his music, creating tracks that resonate deeply with listeners.

Career Beginnings and Breakthroughs:
Mizter Bonezz began his DJ career in 2009 under the alias DJ Gooddan21. His passion for music and innate talent quickly set him apart. He graduated high school in 2011 from Canoga Park Senior High School with a 3.9 GPA and initially pursued an accounting major in college. However, due to deteriorating mental health from untreated bipolar 2 depression, he dropped out in 2013 to fully dedicate himself to music.

In 2019, Mizter Bonezz was discovered by Mandragora after a video of him performing “Codeine” at EDC Las Vegas went viral. This breakthrough led to a signing with Brazil’s Alien Records and a collaboration with Thales Dumbra and Cruzmon VI. He has since become a prominent figure in the psytrance scene, influenced by artists like WADE, Hugel, Mandragora, Vini Vici, and Chapeleiro.

Notable Achievements:

	•	Met and opened for major artists like Skrillex, Steve Aoki, and Wiz Khalifa.
	•	Performed at significant events like DreamState So Cal and supported acts like Coming Soon!!!
	•	Released a 4-song psytrance EP titled “Ayahuasca Village” in May 2024, featuring tracks like “Torment,” “Amnesia,” “Lone Wolf,” and “The Comeback.”
	•	Launched a monthly radio mix show called “Mizter Bonezz Bone Breakin Beatz” on Insomniac Radio, airing every first Tuesday of the month.

Musical Style and Influence:
Mizter Bonezz’s music is characterized by its emotional depth, complex rhythms, and seamless integration of various electronic subgenres. His tracks often feature pulsating basslines, hypnotic rhythms, and ethereal melodies, creating a rich tapestry of sound. His unique style has earned him a dedicated fan base and recognition within the electronic music community.

Personal Life:
Mizter Bonezz’s resilience extends beyond his music career. His mother, affectionately known as “Mama Bonezz,” was diagnosed with stage 4 pancreatic cancer in January 2024 and is undergoing weekly chemotherapy treatments. Despite these personal challenges, Mizter Bonezz continues to inspire others through his music and advocacy.

Impact and Legacy:
Mizter Bonezz’s story is one of perseverance, creativity, and passion. He has not only made a significant impact in the electronic music scene but also serves as an inspiration for those facing their own challenges. His music invites listeners on a journey, reflecting the highs and lows of life and the power of resilience.

With a growing discography and an unwavering commitment to his craft, Mizter Bonezz is poised to continue making waves in the music industry, leaving an indelible mark on those who experience his sound.

"HighBIScus" is a deeply evocative song that weaves together themes of love, life, death, and the intricate relationship between humanity and nature, particularly within an agricultural context. The lyrics paint a vivid picture of a culture embroiled in conflict, where the planting and growing of cannabis become metaphors for resilience, survival, and the cyclical nature of existence.

The opening lines, "You were Mine before the showers, Watered you and gave you power," set the stage for a narrative of nurturing and growth. The metaphorical connection between the protagonist's love and the cultivation of cannabis suggests a symbiotic relationship between human emotions and the natural world. As the song progresses, the lyrics delve into the complexities of life's struggles, juxtaposed with the fragility of existence. The repeated imagery of "Hibiscus flowers" symbolizes both beauty and transience, echoing the fleeting nature of life itself.

Amidst themes of love and growth, the song takes a poignant turn as it addresses the devastating impact of war and loss. Lines like "War torn in a system of culture tradition, They died opposition never changing positions," convey the brutality and futility of conflict, where individuals are caught in cycles of violence and suffering. However, even in the face of tragedy, there's a sense of resilience and reverence for those who have passed, as depicted in the lines, "I place my burden by their halos, Tombstone of their graves, oh lord." Ultimately, "HighBIScus" transcends its reggae roots to become a powerful meditation on the human condition, reminding listeners of the interconnectedness of life, death, and the natural world.

"Swara Sukma Ing Antara" is an electro-horror composition that portrays the inner journey of a soul lost among the shadows of the past. This idea was born in the stillness of midnight, imagining a spirit trapped in shattered memories, filled with regret and despair. To evoke this atmosphere, the piece opens with a repetitive synthesizer sound layered with modulated analog synth distortion, forming a harmony that trembles like fragmented memories. Fragmented melodies from a granular synthesizer emerge like whispers and sobs from the past, as if something unseen is lurking behind the silence.

In the middle of the composition, a hauntingly repetitive pattern from a music box sample and soul-crushing chords appears, depicting the soul’s confrontation with its own unrecognizable shadow. The music reaches its climax through layered, competing dissonances, then collapses into an echoing void and distant screams — a symbol of the soul’s fall into eternal emptiness. Although electronic in nature, this work carries the weight of human emotion, blending horror elements and ambient textures to create a psychological space that invites listeners to confront their own unresolved fears and memories.

BUZZ is one of the most impressive vocalists we’ve heard in the last decade. 

She’s a songwriter with credits on mainstream tracks by Katy Perry, Kylie Minogue, and Bebe Rexha but her own music is closer to pure art.

We first heard her track Liberation — a heart-stopping, stripped-back vocal with only a vocoder synth for texture. It was raw and powerful, signalling the entrance of someone stepping out of the songwriter role in the background and owning the stage as her own. Across the rest of her catalog, BUZZ’s voice effortlessly shifts from pop hooks to almost operatic highs with complete control.

We were lucky enough to work together to bring Liberation onchain and create 12 different remixes from the community. We followed up with Different Sun, and now we’re back with an extremely limited edition of her new single.

There will only be 50 editions of “Left Behind” — another vulnerable and honest track about moving on from her upbringing, letting go of fear and being free in as many ways as possible.

For me, it’s the perfect song to launch our new series of limited editions, where we treat outstanding music moments as works of art. This feels like a turning point for a new artist breaking out and owning her own story.

Hope you like it as much as we do.

Description: Dotr
Bitcoin to the 100. It is my life.

In 2018, underground artist Nuri began crafting "The Bitcoin Song" to commemorate Bitcoin's upcoming 10th anniversary. He wanted to capture the rebellious essence of cryptocurrency, but the song wasn't fully realized until 2023. That year, as the global economic landscape grew more uncertain, Nuri felt the time was right. Working under the production company we named Bitcoin Billionaire Ballers Social Club, which also launched an NFT collection with over 9,000 versions of the track, he perfected "Bitcoin XV 2024" in time for Bitcoin’s 15th anniversary on January 3rd, 2024. The song opens with a bold proclamation of "Bitcoin Billionaire Ballers," signaling the cryptocurrency’s rise from its genesis in 2009 to a revolutionary financial force.

Nuri’s lyrics vividly address Bitcoin’s critics, portraying them as out-of-touch skeptics while celebrating Bitcoin's ability to empower the masses. He raps about flipping the financial script, mocking Wall Street insiders, and emphasizing Bitcoin’s value as fair money for the people. The chorus echoes this sentiment: "Bitcoin, like gold is rare; Bitcoin makes money fair." With references to icons like Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. and James Brown, Nuri connects Bitcoin’s financial revolution to broader struggles for justice. Through "Bitcoin XV 2024," both the song and the NFT collection stand as powerful symbols of Bitcoin’s enduring legacy, celebrating a movement that isn’t going anywhere.

Nuri’s groundbreaking NFT project, launched under the Bitcoin Billionaire Ballers production company, pushed the boundaries of digital art and music in a way that had never been done before. With over 9,000 unique versions of "The Bitcoin Song," the project was designed to commemorate Bitcoin’s 15th anniversary in a monumental fashion. Each NFT version features variations in verses, choruses, beats, and production layers, creating an extensive, one-of-a-kind collection. No other artist had ever created so many distinct versions of a single song, making the project a trailblazer in the NFT space. This innovative concept not only allows fans to own a piece of Bitcoin’s legacy but also personalized the experience by offering an exclusive version for each NFT holder. By combining cutting-edge technology with the revolutionary ethos of cryptocurrency, Bitcoin Billionaire Ballers Social Club NFT collection is redefining how music is experienced, shared, and monetized in the digital age.

A ghostly waltz for the walking wounded, *"Save Yourself"* is Gypsylost’s venom-laced lullaby to codependency, where her signature tarot-card whimsy collides with the brutal reality of love as a bloodsport. The track unfolds like a séance gone wrong—mournful piano keys dissolve into industrial snarls as her voice shifts between haunted-child whispers and the guttural growl of something far older. Lyrics like *"I’ll light your candles if you dig my grave"* aren’t metaphors; they’re autopsy reports from relationships where she played both savior and sacrifice.  

This song was scrawled in the margins of a stolen motel Bible at 3AM, somewhere between Nashville’s neon glow and the Carolina backroads. Gypsylost wrote it after realizing every person she’d ever resurrected had only wanted her bones for their altar. The production mirrors that revelation—church-choir harmonies warp into static, like a radio losing signal mid-prayer. It’s not a breakup song. It’s an exorcism. Press play if you’re ready to watch the pyre consume what you once swore you’d die for.

Poem "LOAM"

I saw a city steeped in endless calm,  
Shattered by time that stretches without end.  
There, wires hum beneath the wind’s wild psalm,  
And windows stare, blind to the void they tend.  

Once, people built their world with dreams of might,  
To rule o’er all that is, their grand design.  
But now their flame is quenched, their reason slight,  
Leaving an echo in the skies’ loud whine.  

Sand and ash weave patterns in the air,  
Footsteps of the past drown in silence deep.  
What did we seek in our mad, fervent prayer?  
Why did we raise these walls so high and steep?  

And in this world where only shadows roam,  
Nature whispers: "All shall return to loam."

OBSESSIVE-COMPULSIVE PERSONALITY DISORDER

Obsessive-compulsive personality disorder (OCPD) is a mental health condition characterized by an extensive preoccupation with perfectionism, order, and control. This preoccupation can significantly interfere with daily life and relationships. Here's a breakdown of its key features:

Core Characteristics:

Excessive Devotion to Orderliness and Rules: Individuals with OCPD have a rigid need for things to be done in a specific way, adhering strictly to rules and routines. This inflexibility can hinder their ability to adapt to change or compromise.
Perfectionism: Unrealistic expectations of perfection in themselves and others can lead to procrastination, difficulty completing tasks, and dissatisfaction with even minor imperfections.
Control Issues: A strong desire to control their environment and the people around them can create tension and strain in relationships. They may be reluctant to delegate tasks or trust others to do things their way.
Emotional Detachment: Difficulty expressing emotions freely and forming close relationships due to their preoccupation with control and perfectionism.

Symptoms:

Excessive devotion to work, often neglecting leisure activities or relationships.
Fixation of details, lists, and schedules, losing sight of the bigger picture.
Difficulty discarding possessions, even those of no value, due to a fear of needing them later.
Unwillingness to spend money unless absolutely necessary.
Stubbornness and inflexibility in their thinking and behavior.
Difficulty delegating tasks or collaborating with others.
Differences from Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD):

While both involve a preoccupation with order and control, they are distinct conditions:

Focus: In OCD, the focus is on intrusive thoughts and repetitive behaviors driven by anxiety to reduce distress. In OCPD, the focus is on maintaining control and orderliness, often driven by a sense of righteousness and moral correctness.
Distress: Individuals with OCD often experience significant distress due to their intrusive thoughts and compulsions. Those with OCPD may not recognize their behavior as problematic and may even derive a sense of satisfaction from their rigid routines.

Impact and Treatment:

OCPD can significantly impact personal and professional life:

Difficulty maintaining healthy relationships.
Work-related problems due to inflexibility and inefficiency.
Social isolation due to emotional detachment.

Treatment options for OCPD include:

Psychotherapy: Techniques like cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) can help individuals challenge their rigid thinking patterns and develop more flexible coping mechanisms.
Medications: In some cases, antidepressants like selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) may be used to manage associated anxiety or depression.
Remember, seeking professional help is crucial for individuals with OCPD to manage their symptoms and improve their overall well-being.

Online Resources:

The International OCD Foundation (IOCDF): https://iocdf.org/
provides comprehensive information about OCPD, including support groups, treatment options, and fact sheets.

The OCPD Foundation: https://iocdf.org/wp-content/uploads/2014/10/OCPD-Fact-Sheet.pdf 

offers resources specifically dedicated to OCPD, including information, support groups, and educational materials.

HelpGuide.org: https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/24526-obsessive-compulsive-personality-disorder-ocpd 

provides a clear and concise overview of OCPD, including symptoms, treatment options, and self-help tips.

Additional Tips:

Educate Yourself: Understanding the nature of OCPD can be helpful for both individuals with the condition and their loved ones.
Seek Professional Help: Early intervention and therapy can significantly improve the quality of life for people with OCPD.
Join a Support Group: Connecting with others facing similar challenges can provide valuable support and understanding.
Be Patient: Change takes time and effort. Celebrate small victories and focus on gradual progress.
Remember, seeking help is a sign of strength, not weakness. With the right support and resources, individuals with OCPD can learn to manage their symptoms and build fulfilling lives.

Description:
XYSM: I made the beat for this track while on a trip across Canada. All I had at the time was a cheap 2011 laptop I bought off of a friend for a couple hundred bucks. This computer didn't have enough room to download half of the software I use to make music and so I was incredibly limited in what I was able to do.

Sometimes being limited is a good thing though. It forces you to be creative, and if you asked me to recreate that beat, there would be no chance that I could do it, A lot of the sounds that seem like synthesizers are just vocals, chopped and transposed to a point where it is unrecognizable. That's why I love this track so much, it has all these unique sounds that came from a little laptop with barely anything on it. 

A couple months later, this track then became 'Body Talkin' after a writing session with Lindal and our friend Rocky Raccoon. We kept the song's vintage feel by pitching down Lindal's vocals, which also gave it a smooth RnB feel.

"U.(S.AD)" by Mr.FLEN is a hard-hitting critique of America's current socio-political landscape. This grime-influenced track takes listeners on a journey through economic struggles, political disillusionment, and the everyday reality of the working class. Mr.FLEN tackles major issues like skyrocketing inflation, the broken healthcare system, and the growing wealth gap, all while delivering sharp, biting lyrics that leave nothing off the table.

With powerful imagery and relentless flow, Mr.FLEN points fingers at the bipartisan blame game in Washington, where both Democrats and Republicans are too wrapped up in their own power plays to address the real issues affecting Americans. The chorus highlights the frustration felt by many: the dollar’s value plummeting, politicians moving too slow, and ordinary people bearing the brunt of these failures.

In his second verse, Mr.FLEN further exposes the divide between Wall Street's booming profits and Main Street's pain, where families are struggling just to survive while banks and corporations thrive. The interlude is a reflective moment, calling out the repetitive nature of political games and demanding real change, urging listeners to rise up against complacency.

The final verse shifts focus to the climate crisis, rising crime, and the hollow narratives pushed by mainstream media, reinforcing the idea that the true fight lies in the hands of everyday people. Mr.FLEN’s clever wordplay and grim outlook provide a gritty yet truthful commentary on the state of the nation, with a clear call for action by the track’s conclusion.

"U.(S.AD)" is more than just a song—it's a raw depiction of America’s current struggles, wrapped in gritty grime beats and relentless bars that refuse to let the listener stay complacent. The title itself reflects the sadness of the state of the U.S. (United States), a nation that once stood tall, now battling deep fractures within.

Perfect for fans of politically charged music like Dave or Skepta, Mr.FLEN gives a voice to the voiceless, calling out the systems in power that need to be held accountable.

The Story:

"Dive" was written, recorded, produced, mixed and mastered by Mikey Maramag (Blackbird Blackbird) in Montréal, Canada, circa March 2024. Lyrics by Mikey Maramag.

Feelings can crystallize so deeply & intensely that at first it feels like you are diving into a vast sea of love, or an 'ocean of love', as the lyrics portray in the second verse (one of my personal favorite parts of any song I've ever done).

The intro hook "Don't worry, I'll catch you if you fall", foreshadows the drama of the second chorus, and refers to the initial feeling of uncertainty of the start of a relationship. 

Diving straight in to something real, with barely any time to test the waters is scary at first, but sometimes love comes in a rush of moments and happens so fast that it takes over your entire world in no time at all. 

Throughout the song I wanted to play around with space. The intro starts dry and trots along, kind of symbolizing where I was at in life & reflecting on the difficulty I had in finding a love that wasn't toxic or superficial. 

Then the gentle guitar plucks come in and glue things together playfully, sparking an ambition & building curiosity. Only through self-care and bettering myself was I able to be alone and content with myself, which is also what happened right before I met my true love, and gave me fortitude & strength to accept this love.

There is also a kind of kinophobia, or fear of open spaces (which I personally suffer from sometimes) that I wanted to address in structure and feel of the song. In contrast to this feeling, love bridges distances, brings people closer, and acts like a warm light or radiance, like something familiar--something that feels like home. Hopefully the song can do this for you as well.

The buildup right before the drop into the synth-driven, abyssal ocean that is the chorus, I wanted it to feel like the listener is catching their breath & getting ready to 'Dive' in!

Meeting your true love can feel like a religious experience, a moment of awe, or an instant cure-all for the nihilistic loneliness & dystopia of modern dating life. But there are always challenges in a relationship or partnership, and I wanted to express the mutual feeling of being there for each other to catch each other, in case either of us falls down, we'll help each other get back up.

I guess I just thought, why not just put all these different conflicting emotions of love together and write a song about it. Dive is what I came up with. I hope it can help others find both true love and SELF-LOVE, and regardless of what they are going through I'm happy to have it out in the world & hope you enjoy! :)

Love,
Mikey

The final single from Spectres channels the Anima, which Jung defined as "an archetypal image of woman in the male psyche... a pervasive influence in a man’s life. The anima is the archetype of life itself."

Comprising 13 experimental tracks produced over the last seven years, Spectres is the 28th release in my discography but my first ever completely solo full-length album. While working on this record, I delved deep into Jungian psychology, concepts from which became central to the project. All 13 tracks are named after archetypes—innate, universal forces that shape our experience of the world.

Spectres is also a visual art project. For each track, I crowd-sourced images associated with the corresponding archetype. These image collections were used to train bespoke Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), simulating the complex interplay between individual psyche and collective unconscious. A further GAN was trained on selected outputs from all the previous GANs, uniting the various archetypes to form an integrated Self.

By limiting the training time of these AI models, I found I could achieve results that mirrored the formation of archetypal symbols as I imagine them deep in our collective unconscious: elusive yet powerful forms emerging from abstract swirls of colour. From thousands of outputs, I selected and manually edited one per archetype to create unique artworks for each track. A collection of 144 further images from this project dropped under the title Spectral Shadows.

Ultimately, Spectres is more than a collection of WAVs and JPGs; it is a dialogue between the personal and the universal, a multidisciplinary exploration of the forces that connect us all. The album has taken me on a transformative seven-year journey through sound, imagery and psyche. In the process, individual and collective experience harmonise, casting a light into the profound depths of human interconnectedness.

“#97BCEB” by WarBaby of Outside The Wire Productions is a true testament to raw human expression—a one-of-a-kind digital asset that can never be replicated by AI or machines. 

This NFT captures the organic, hand-crafted artistry that emerged from the depths of personal experience. Each sound and layer was crafted “from scratch,” reflecting the intense emotions born from WarBaby’s time in the U.S. Army, especially during high-stakes moments in the Middle East. Music became a mental escape from the chaos around him, transforming adrenaline and inner conflict into powerful soundscapes. 

The audio was professionally and delicately designed, using specific frequencies chosen to heal through sound, frequency, and vibration. This timeless piece of artwork is not only unique; it stands as a tribute to the resilience and authenticity that only human touch can create.

In the realm of my tumultuous love affair with the music industry, I am trying to paint a vivid picture through the metaphor of a romantic relationship and drug addiction. Picking up the industry from its metaphorical class, armed with roses and candy symbolizing my passion and dedication, my optimism is shattered when I discover the industry kissing another man, representing the betrayals and challenges I faces. The chorus, "I'll Never Learn," becomes a poignant mantra echoing the cyclic nature of my struggles. The lyrics delve into the paradox of the industry, likening it to a demanding partner that never reciprocates as much as it takes. I am caught in the addictive cycle, narrating the highs and lows, using vivid imagery and wordplay to convey the complexities of my relationship. The story unfolds as I grapple with the toll it takes on my mental well-being, resorting to substances as a coping mechanism. Despite the hardships, the allure of the music industry persists, leaving me ensnared in a cycle of addiction and creative passion, ultimately resigning myself to the perpetual refrain of "I'll Never Learn."

I MANIFEST, from Symbolik's Breadth Of Existence album, is an offering of ancient cultural expression, observational commentary, and Hip Hop poetry. Inspired by the Kemetic tree of life research and a community call to depict and represent the balance that exists between the cosmic, spirittual and Geb the physical.

I MANIFEST is the result of an international collaboration with Symbolik (Toronto, Canada) and Webber from Yin Sang (Beijing, China), and represents the universal nature of Hip Hop.

I MANIFEST was originally released in a limited capacity in 2007, and reflects the influence of the era that is known as "True School" Hip Hop, where lyricism, deeper meanings and social impact where core to the Hip Hop form.

The artist Symbolik gained experience, knowledge and a sense of self from the global Hip Hop movement. While he has worked in the media/interactive media and communications space, and went on to earn his BFA and Masters in Fine Arts and Interactive Production, Symbolik always considered Hip Hop his first and most foundational training ground.

Symbolik believes that music, art and social empowerment onchain is an amazing new way to express, support and vote for what we, love and want to see more of in the world. Symbolik is excited to release I MANIFEST on Sound.xyz and is confident this collectible will look and sound great in your wallet!

Velvet Meadow brings a new FUNKY flare to his sound with new single "Its My Fault". During the writing phase of this track, Heironimus wanted to experiment with writing something with some groove and soul into it. The track was written in his rented out room in St Augustine Florida shortly after gaining inspiration from some of vintage R&B soul records he picked up from a nearby flea market. Upon release, it has become a staple in his discography gaining over 4k streams its first week, with a continuous climb. 

"I wanted to write something that is a little out of my comfort zone. I wanted something more upbeat, and more upfront strong vocals with a little cheekiness to it. Its got to be one of my favorite pop tunes I have written. I just kind of jumped into the deep with it writing, and production wise. My favorite aspect of it is the counter melody in the chorus thing spouting its my fault. I also love the ending with the synthesizers getting super trippy. I am a huge synth head, always will be. I was super stoked it did so well, as I thought it would be a lot more niche in the psych pop world than it is." Kris Heironimus

Thank you to everyone supporting the project. It means the world to me I have so many supporters and all around groovy people in this community. You guys are the backbone of this project. If you are new to the project, welcome to the Meadow. <3

Llévame is rooted in one of the most intensely personal and transformative experiences of my life. During a trip to Amsterdam with a close friend, the city’s energy and the effects of magic mushrooms brought us closer in every possible way. The connection was wild, raw, and unapologetically physical. We completely surrendered to the moment, exploring each other with no reservations, letting go of everything but the sensations we shared.

The lyrics reflect that passion—lines like “Hasta el fondo de tu ser” aren’t just poetic. They’re a reflection of how deeply we connected, both physically and emotionally. With every thrust, her body responded, and the more I pushed, the more she let go, completely giving in to the moment. Each time we came together, her body unable to contain the intensity. The experience was mutual—an exchange of raw pleasure and connection. We lost ourselves in it, pushing the boundaries of what we thought possible.

The video blends reality with surreal elements, mirroring the hallucinatory state we were in. Just like the experience, it’s a mix of the real and the dreamlike, taking the viewer through that journey of physical and emotional surrender. It’s a visual and auditory trip that reflects the raw essence of what happened that night.

This week, we rolled out an upgrade to stories on OnchainMagic to make them an ERC1155 instead of an ERC721. This saves 77% of gas costs. Our goal is to make it stupid simple for creators to put content on Zora. The challenge with our first iteration of stories was cost to deploy & ease of use filling the wallet.

How can we drive down the cost of the everyday user? Both the amount of money they spend, the time and the energy they spend to put moments and memories onchain. With our original use of Zora ERC721 drops on OP Mainnet cost about 0.001 ETH or about $1.50 with creators earning, 0.000444 ETH on free mints. They need to mint approximately three additions to break even.

While this is way better than Ethereum Mainnet, where the costs are like $10 - 20 to deploy a contract. We still have a lot further to go. And so, what did we get by switching to the ERC1155?

The cost to deploy a new ERC1155 is 0.0005 ETH. It's already about 50% less than deploying an ERC721 on OP mainnet. If you want to add a new story to an existing collection, it's 0.0003 ETH, which is about 25% of the cost to deploy a ERC721 on OP Mainnet. AKA a reduction of 75% from the ERC721A. And it's significantly less than the cost to deploy an equivalent ERC721 on Ethereum Mainnet.

And so, at this point, if you sell one edition, you earn 0.00444 ETH

This allows our costs to be low enough for local communities to subsidize gas fees because at this point for a creator they're earning right out the gate 0.0001 ETH in revenue for a story that they would not have earned for on Instagram.

So how can we make it really easy to refill the wallet for the first time? We also rolled out auto-refill for creators. So if you're about to create a post or a story and you don't have enough energy or ETH or fuel or gas, we automatically refill your wallet.

This eliminated, one of the most challenging parts which was funding the social wallet. All of this is enabling our creators who have never used Zora before to upload content directly from live music events. What are the dashboards we need to build to measure the few specific outcomes that we're optimizing for? And if you're going to post on Instagram, why not post it as a story onchain as well?

ABOUT SPIRIT AWAY

Spirit Away is about the self-reflection that occurs post-relationship.

In this case, it’s about me looking in the mirror, seeing the crows feet around my eyes, a few gray hairs, and wondering, "Do I still have what it takes to pursue what I want in life or am I kidding myself?"

I imagine a lot of people go through this at some point in life, perhaps multiple times. Spirit Away is simply me acknowledging when those feelings arise. If someone listens to it and can relate, at least they’ll know they aren’t alone.


SOME EXCERPTS

“Who is this? Looking back at me?
The creases in his eyes try not to lie
but can’t help talking through the steam and
he knows talk is cheap."

It’s sobering when I realize that while I’ve put countless reps into pursuing what I want in life, there’s still plenty of times when I’ve been all talk. I know that the solution is in the reps, so that when the opportunities (or luck, however you want to frame it) come along, I’ll be prepared for them, but I’m also 40 years old. As much as I believe age is simply a number, there’s a different level of self-doubt that surfaces as I get older. It’s odd, like simultaneously living between confidence with age and self-doubt with age.


“And he’s had love, but not the lasting kind.
Like a rolling stone, he has big dreams,
but can’t quite seem to see clearly that
the moss you gather’s fine."

I’ve come to realize the culmination of experiences I’ve had, both in love and life pursuits, are just those — experiences. Rather than viewing them as failures of where I should have turned left instead of right, I now try my best to view them as a stone that has gathered moss, but the moss is a defining feature of the stone, and what gives it character while on its journey.


“It’s like I’m waiting on everything I’m chasing
to come and spirit me away from here."

I used to live in Japan, and while many people know of the beautiful movie Spirited Away, it’s the concept of being spirited away that inspired me for this set of lyrics. I feel like the concept of someone vanishing and returning at a later time is a part of Japanese folk lore — enough to where there’s terminology for it, 神隠し (kami kakushi) — in a way that I haven’t seen in the United States. Indeed, the best translation seems to be spirited away. In the case of the lyrics, I’m trying to convey that it often feels like I’m waiting for something to happen, some magic spirit from my goals to take me where I want to go, and in doing so, have missed opportunities, either from a lack of putting in the reps or lack of being proactive.


OTHER INTERESTING NOTES

Spirit Away (as well as the whole EP) was co-produced by me (Mike Bass), Alara, and Steven LaFashia. This was my first time working with other producers, and enjoyed the process very much!

Spirit Away features an incredible singer-songwriter, musician, and friend, Emma Miller. The beautiful background/harmony vocals you hear that give the song another depth of life are done by Emma.

The Branches EP was recorded at Retro City Studios in Philadelphia, PA.

Spirit Away blends more into the indie-folk genre, which is new for me. The same goes for the EP as a whole, which has dream pop, indie folk, and even indie pop elements.

records.title: Black Water (with San Holo & Lizzy Land)

Description:
San Holo and I wrote the beat together, mostly around some piano parts that re recorded live. It had a few different toplines on it, but I sent it to Lizzy Land because I thought her tone would work perfectly for it. We were talking about imperfection and how to embrace that. Black Water itself represents a metaphor for the realisation that you can find most of the answers to life’s questions from looking inward rather than out.

"It was an amazing experience to work with musicians as talented as Daktyl and Lizzy Land! Getting to create with artists that I love is such an honor, and I'm so happy with how the song turned out." - San Holo

"Black Water is about having all the answers you need inside. In your darkest moments, when you feel alone without hope, there is this pool of infinite, eternal knowing that spills out in front of you. A mirror reflecting what you already know back to you.

Daktyl and I wrote “black water” while talking about expectations. The idea that perfect does and doesn’t exist. Like nature or the night sky. Imperfection is a human opinion and ultimately you hold the key to your own happiness.” - Lizzy Land

Walking down the street I saw the first snow,
And I realized, we are all dead snowflakes.
And here and there, they are already lying,
Reminding us, of the frailty of this life.

They are born in the sky and fly.
Free and at liberty to live as they wish.
Having accelerated their run, they circle faster,
Like people, in the recklessness of gray days.

And they die... they die, one way or another...
Some will remain nothing, never waking up.
Others, something... But they won't be cried for either.

Children will sculpt fortresses and build slides.
Throw corpses of snowflakes, with frozen hands.
They will paint snowdrifts yellow, different lapdogs, Yorkies...
And the same children will touch them with frozen lips.

But winter will end, and sooner or later,
The janitors will rake up the snowflakes, ending their short life.
And so that in the spring, having become a dirty puddle,
They could turn back into dead snow in winter...

Sara and I met back in September of 2023 at a concert for our mutual friend TAROT. Sara was also performing that night and I heard in person how talented she was. I had heard about her because of our other mutual friend DOT, who I've remixed before on "Follow Me," and Dot herself just had released a remix of Sara's song "Hurts." I thought it would be a good idea to expand my network naturally and talked to Sara after the show to see if she would be interested in a collaboration, considering we had already collaborated with a few of the same people. She expressed interest in the collaboration, and I spent the next few months crafting some ideas to send to her.

In the beginning of the new year, I had an instrumental done that I knew would be a perfect fit for Sara's voice, and when I sent it to her she expressed enthusiasm for the idea and began working on writing to it immediately. Over the next couple months we exchanged ideas back and forth until we arrived at "Miss It," a unique but somewhat nostalgic summertime house track that we both really loved. I loved my experience working with Sara, she's extremely talented (and funny) and she has a rare ability to take any song and make it the best it can possibly be.

This is only my 2nd ever drop on Soundxyz, and I don't think I could have chosen a better collaborator than one of the shining lights and ambassadors of the platform. I'm hoping to expand my reach and community on this platform in the coming months and years, as I truly believe in its powers and capabilities for independent artists, but for now, let this drop be the start of something big! Huge thanks to everyone who collects!

“I initially meant for this song to be about a codependent friendship. I began writing this as a way to understand my friends perspective in our relationship and how they grew to be so overly dependent on me. But what really happened is as I finally got all the lyrics together for the song and examined them from a birds eye view was that the song was more of a reflection of how both of our tendancies nurtured this codependency, meaning there wasn’t one single party to blame. Melodramatic is about holding up a mirror to our toxic relationships and coming to terms with the role we play in keeping them alive, because people can’t latch themselves on to you if you don’t extend an arm out as well.“

I think you are constantly looking for what that next inspiration to write a record will be… never knowing if today or tomorrow will be the day you find that moment or idea that makes you realize what it is you want to say.

"How am I to be creative? Nature knows only one answer to that: Through a child (the gift of love)." (Jung)

The next single from Spectres deals with the archetype of the Child, which Jung called "an image of both the irrecoverable past and an anticipation of future development." Furthermore, he wrote that "In every adult there lurks a child–an eternal child, something that is always becoming, is never completed, and calls for unceasing care, attention, and education. That is the part of the personality which wants to develop and become whole."

Comprising 13 experimental tracks produced over the last seven years, Spectres is the 28th release in my discography but my first ever completely solo full-length album. While working on this record, I delved deep into Jungian psychology, concepts from which became central to the project. All 13 tracks are named after archetypes—innate, universal forces that shape our experience of the world.

Spectres is also a visual art project. For each track, I crowd-sourced images associated with the corresponding archetype. These image collections were used to train bespoke Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), simulating the complex interplay between individual psyche and collective unconscious. A further GAN was trained on selected outputs from all the previous GANs, uniting the various archetypes to form an integrated Self.

By limiting the training time of these AI models, I found I could achieve results that mirrored the formation of archetypal symbols as I imagine them deep in our collective unconscious: elusive yet powerful forms emerging from abstract swirls of colour. From thousands of outputs, I selected and manually edited one per archetype to create unique artworks for each track. A collection of 144 further images from this project dropped under the title Spectral Shadows.

Ultimately, Spectres is more than a collection of WAVs and JPGs; it is a dialogue between the personal and the universal, a multidisciplinary exploration of the forces that connect us all. The album has taken me on a transformative seven-year journey through sound, imagery and psyche. In the process, individual and collective experience harmonise, casting a light into the profound depths of human interconnectedness.

Before its official release on 11/23, I'm rolling Spectres out across the web3 ecosystem, with drops on Sound, Zora, Rodeo, Lens and other emerging platforms. In a novel release structure, collectors of individual tracks gain instant access to stream the full album months before its official release. The goal is to push the limits of onchain interoperability to explore what a web3-native album release can look like in 2024.

This song originated in Nashville, TN when Max (yadzi) was visiting from LA and staying at my house for the weekend! (one could say that's where the inspo for the words 'guest + house' came from, but it was actually directly inspired by the poem 'Guest House' by Rumi)

'Guest House' is about learning how to live with, and furthermore, welcome in, your emotions. Feelings aren't necessarily a new topic for me, as I often speak on mental health in my music, but the exploring & recreating of the production alongside Max, was very refreshing. I met Max through Songcamp/headless CHAOS, which has truly proven to be the gift that keeps on giving.

We hope this song finds the collectors + listeners who need it, and remind them that they're not alone in their feelings. And there is always time to make friends with your emotions.. I'm still learning how to do that everyday. 

Thank you to Reveel + Decent, for this sick opportunity.. You guys are all true champions of art/creators.

I think this song is the perfect selection for my web3 music Genesis. This is a super fun song I made early last summer (2022). The whole thing came together really quickly from a writing and production standpoint, but wrapping it up and putting it out was a different story. 

My life in art and music up to this point has always been in service of this growing feeling of anxiousness from within my nervous system. The easiest way to satisfy it has been to create things (and occasionally destroy them). When I satisfy it, everything gets quiet and feels at peace. When it isn't satiated, it feels like frenetic energy surging through my system, that will certainly end in disaster.

Sometimes my inner voice isn't on my side, and all I can do is remind myself I am still in charge.

There's probably a lot to unpack there in itself, but this blurb is about SPLIT. So for me, this song is about finding clarity and peace when perhaps all you feel are confusion and chaos. It's about finding motivation through a chorus of doubt. It is special for me, and I really hope you find something in it that will be special for you too.

For my genesis Sound drop it was important to stay true to the essence. I could’ve gone with another style of music but it was key for me to make history by sticking to the roots. When I first got into crypto in 2017, I noticed that the majority of the artists involved were in electronic music, a culture I was also a part of but I knew it would be an uphill battle to get Reggaeton recognition in the space. Fast-forward a few years and I accomplished everything I set out too in crypto/web3. (so far)

I made this song late 2021, I was on a hot streak knocking down about 3 records a night and “SOLTERA” was born. I needed a dope Reggaeton for the INFINXTE album and this was the one. The track is produced by two of my closest friends, Los Hitmen, a grammy-nominated production duo that have worked with heavyweights like J Balvin, Jay Wheeler, and De La Ghetto. I remember as soon as I sent the track I got a call back right away like “WTF DID YOU DO HERE?!” I knew right then we had a hit. 

The original artwork was crafted by one of my favorite artists from Spain, Diego (Paranoidme). I think one of the most exciting parts of my album is the diversity in collaborators, its completely organic and features artists from more than ten countries. Reggaeton was rejected in the mainstream for years and now its the voice of the youth all over Latin America, the Caribbean and people all over the world. Reggaeton pushes culture forward and I want to push it forward into web3.

There are two friends that I've known since I was less than a year old. We formed a music band together, and then one moved out to the Pyrenees mountains while we were still kids. We stayed close friends though.

And as I started making electronic music, he would listen to my songs every weekend or so, encouraging me in the process. All my songs were similar to each other and not well refined, but I had this one thing that I was trying to create over and over.

About 8 years later we were back together in the countryside, where we grew up, and I played "Ten Thirty Seven", a song made in 2023. I told him "it's the same music I've been trying to make since we were teens", and he replied "yes, but it's getting better". So this is the latest version of my one thing.

MAXIM PERUMAL

We live and we die, our atoms never disappearing just changing form over and over - into the dust under our feet.

Our palaces of stone will not protect us from our death or our bodies decay.  Us mammals covered in hair that rail against our aging, our inevitable death and yet all that came before is already dust and we will go to meet those atoms soon enough.

I once made a ceramic pot and returned it to the wild to be washed away by the rain - a friend said to me “I wonder if that clay will ever remember it was a pot” 

Just dust and hair.

While the origin of the Hoodenza is the subject of great speculation, the monks have  a sacred responsibility to protect an ancient knowledge.  The teachings and practices of this secretive order have been kept closely guarded for centuries, only bits and pieces of the knowledge has been shared with mankind.  


The Hoodenza monks train in secret, isolated from the rest of the known world, engaged in extreme meditative practices.  All trainees undergo rigorous mental and physical disciplines in order to prepare their bodies and minds for receiving the knowledge transmitted from the ether.  


The Hoodenza lived a life of extreme asceticism, practicing martial arts, meditation, and various forms of physical and mental disciplines that would seem barbaric by the standards of modern man. They were forbidden from marrying, having children, or forming any attachments to the outside world.  The monks trained for the sole purpose of working with the life-force within the Breath of Life - a trained Hoodenza monks controlled the power to both give and take away life with the breath.  As a collective unit, the Hoodenza controlled a force unparalleled in the world.

For centuries, the Hoodenza remained hidden from the world, living in their mountain fortress, deep in the heart of a remote and treacherous wilderness. Many tried to seek the Hoodenza to learn this power for themselves, however they were known to only a select few, and even then, only by reputation and rumor.

I just got back from a 10-day trip to LA, and while I was there I made some songs w my brokis. Teddy Roxpin is on all the tracks, plus we got Hark Madley, Smile High, and Horace Bray on one song each as well. All these videos were recorded during the demo phase of creation, and document the imperfect process behind the final, shiny master files that might end up on your Discover Weekly one day.

In one clip you'll see me taking my first crack at recording a topline idea, in another Mork n Teddy are modulating synths, and in others Smiley and Horace are channeling ideas straight from dome to instrument. Looking back, what mattered the most about these sessions was getting to express my inner Truth alongside my good friends. It was a very healing experience, and I'm grateful I got to have it.

This trip will always be dear to my heart, in large part because it was my first time visiting LA where I was there for the friendship more than for the city itself. In the 8 years since I started going to LA, this trip marked my most stark shift in perception of it. In a city focused on fame, fortune, and external validation (nothing inherently wrong with that), I experienced a lot of personal relief to find myself effortlessly focused on inner presence over extracting its outer accolades.

Because of this natural evolution in my values, I feel like I'm at the precipice of a new phase in my artistic expression and world creation. I'm glad to have these artifacts up on chain to look back upon. 

Thanks for witnessing my process ! 
What do you notice within your OWN inner landscape in this very moment ? 
And - which one of these songs do YOU want to hear finished first ??

With love,
Forrest

records.title: Terraforms by Mathcastles Explained: Onchain land art from a dynamically generated 3D world (Open Edition)

Description:
This video was created to help newcomers enter and understand the world of Terraforms by Mathcastles. The video was created by Matto during the production process of Hypercastle Explorers, a community extension project built on Terraforms to create a Unity game engine SDK for the project. The video is a snapshot of a moment in the history of Terraforms and the emerging scene around Mathcastles and runtime art.

----

Terraforms by Mathcastles Explained: Onchain land art from a dynamically generated 3D world (Open Edition)

This talk was originally written to accompany an exhibition at NFTBerlin in May of 2022. In it, I seek to provide a concise view of the Terraforms artwork by the Mathcastles studio along with a bit of information about our related project Hypercastle Explorers. Importantly, Terraforms are relatively deep and complex and so for a longer and more detailed Terraforms explainer, I’ve linked to the community slide deck in the video description.

Terraforms is an NFT project by the studio Mathcastles which consists of 0x113d and xaltgeist, two anonymous developers. The project consists of 11,000 NFTs which the developers describe as onchain land art from a dynamically generated on-chain 3D world.

Terraforms can be engaged in multiple ways. At a base level, each token is a piece of animated art rendered on a 32x32 grid of text characters, stored in an SVG file. The animated art is drawn in a web browser using javascript to change the colors and cycle characters of a custom made font.

Each token contains properties including Zone, Biome and Chroma. There are 75 different “Zones” which correspond to color palettes and 92 Biomes which refer to which text characters or shapes the grid for the animation. The Chroma property governs the speed of the cycling of the animation. The combination of these properties gives the collection depth and variation and in my opinion gives an appealing diversity to Terraforms overall. While many generative art collections choose to issue smaller editions of for example 500 tokens, Terraforms can be seen as something of a response to the NFT meta trend of 10,000 unit generative profile pictures pioneered byCrypto Punks. The collection seems to pose an answer to the question: how does one create a generative art collecti on with 11,000 pieces that feels rich, varied and not repetitive?

In addition to appreciating Terraforms as individual art works, they also can be approached as a single fractionalized work of invisible art. Along with its internal characteristics each token is also assigned structural metadata which are displayed in its name: Level 11 at 18,6 for example. This data situates each token as a part of a larger 3D structure informally referred to as the hypercastle. The hypercastle has 20 vertical levels and narrows to a point at the top and bottom, with the widest points at levels 13 and 14. Importantly, each token also contains structural information about it’s internal elevation, in which the visible shapes in the 2d artwork correspond to elevations in a three dimensional map. This structural information is encoded in the smart contract of each token and can therefore be referenced and reproduced by calling the tokens functions on-chain. 

In addition to functioning as both a 2D and 3D artwork, Terraforms also is a functional software tool in which each token can be transformed into a kind of drawing program which overwrites the existing Terrain artwork. The tokens have three modes, Terrain whicccch displays the land art animation, Daydream which enables a user to draw on it and Terraform mode which commits the drawing back to the blockchain for others to view. Transitioning from Terrain to Daydream mode is a destructive operation and cannot be reverted, but a Terraform can be transitioned at will from Daydream to Terraform and vice versa, overwriting and committing new drawings to the chain.

This idea, of Terraforms as an artwork with both visible and invisible layers, stored on a public and permissionless database which anyone can read from and interact with is a new and compelling one. It feels like a truly blockchain native work of art which seeks to deeply explore the possibilities of this technology as an artistic medium. The approach of building a minimalist but beautiful, durable skeleton creates a kind of aesthetic negative space which encourages other artists and explorers to join in and engage with it. Until the fairly recent creation of blockchains and publicly shared but privately ownable computer environments like Ethereum a work of art like this wouldn’t have been possible, and it wouldn’t have been possible for people like us to build alongside it. Through the development of this new technology and the arts and culture around it, new possibilities are emerging and we look forward to exploring them together.

Deep in the Dark Forest of Agony, a crowd of mages gathered around a strange stone door. Each unsuccessfully trying a mix of brute force and spells to open it.  

Eventually, a mage known as Okot came forward. The key dangling around their neck began to shimmer and glow. Before they could even attempt to try the key, a horrid sound erupted. The scraping of stone against stone. Soon, the door was open.

  Inside, there lay a dark room made of nothing but slabs of stone. At the center, a pile of ash. A small sparkle amidst the ash caught Okot's eye.  

Cautiously, Okot moved closer and signaled with a raised hand for the others to stay back.

  Reaching into the ash, they lifted up a scorched silver mask. It bore the markings for the aura & vision of The Grave.

Okot ushered the other mages to come closer. A realization hits anyone looking at it – this mask clearly belonged to a member of The Council.

records.title: NEYBORS Music Video - Heno. featuring Elujay & J.Robb

Description:
Without further ado, Heno. is back with the music video for his song "NEYBORS" with Elujay & J.Robb. With it’s feel-good melodies & catchy lyrics over groovy production, NEYBORS has quickly become a hit in both Web3 & the traditional music world. The video is also a testament to Heno.'s unique creative vision; as well as his ability to seamlessly blend music & storytelling into a powerful experience.

The visually stunning & thought-provoking video (shot by The Reggies) follows a three-part short film that Heno. released entitled "IN THE MEANTIME" about surveillance, therapy, & the lengths one goes through to find peace. In an attempt to find relief, Heno. finds himself going to a kickback as a form of escapism. The record takes you on a thrilling journey through a seemingly normal kickback that quickly turns sinister. 

The short film + this video all serve as a prelude for Heno.'s next project, "I'M TIRED OF BEING HYPERSURVEILLED".

I spent time in the studio reflecting on my childhood, dreams and future. I found myself writing about my inner-dialogue and how I process the high’s and lows within my career as an artist. I’m learning self-love and patience. I’m learning to listen to the voice within that continues to push me forward. I hope this song does the same for you. 

"But I'm alright, I'll find myself"

The Hoodenza is a secret order of monks who lived for millennia in isolation and seclusion from the rest of the world, devoting their lives to their sacred study and practice . Only from whispers has anyone ever heard of the Hoodenza monks, their strict discipline, rigorous training, and unwavering devotion to their sacred science, living with single-pointed concentration on their purpose.

The origins of the Hoodenza are shrouded in mystery, with many legends and myths surrounding their creation. Some say that they were founded by a legendary monk who discovered the ancient teachings of a long-forgotten civilization. Others believe they were founded by a group of ether-spirits called The Immortals, who reside in the non-physical realms of being.  And of course, there are some who don't believe the Hoodenza even exist at all.

It is said that all present day knowledge is fragmented from one source, and that it was the Hoodenza who are the true record keepers of the fates and history of humanity. The Hoodenza watched from afar, the rise and fall of countless empires, dedicating their lives only to a single purpose: to protect and preserve the universal energy field known as "The Breath of Life", which is responsible for all activity in the field of matter. The only times in the history of mankind that anyone has ever seen or heard of the Hoodenza, is when there is a major disturbance in the Breath of Life.

Ever since moving to Los Angeles I've had the pleasure of doing a bunch of sessions with talented vocalists. The process has taught me how to be comfortable in a room and make people feel ready to record, all while trying to be quick on my feet as a producer and catch a vibe with the artist I'm working with.

Over the past few months I've realized that most of the music I've made has been in sessions. And while I love vocal-driven music, I haven't really had the chance to sit back and do my own instrumental production experiments. When I look back on how I got started in music, so much of it was by myself sitting in a room twisting knobs and making odd sounds.

Honey is me taking a step back in that direction - it's a science experiment of a song that serves as my reminder to let go and have fun producing and to not take myself so seriously.

Over the past few months I felt the need to step out of my comfort zone. If you're familiar with my music you'd probably know that I am an electronic music producer, but why should I limit myself to that? 
This is a special song, very different from what I usually put out.
No drums, no "drops", just a piano and a few pads.

Helping Ukraine is not a fashionable thing to do, and it must be persisted in.

Description:
This open-edition mint is a digital collectible produced in collaboration with Zora, who filmed and edited the accompanying video. The video explores the ethos and creative process of Kate the Cursed and will be available to mint for free for one week only. This video is released in conjunction with Kate the Cursed's latest authenticated digital artwork, “human touch” — more information about Kate's NFT open edition, as well as the other artists involved in the QMoDA Artist Grant Program, can be found at Qmoda.art.

Kate the Cursed is one of 10 artists who received a funding grant from QMoDA in January 2023. The full roster of artists is Daniel Oropeza, Kate The Cursed, Dawnia Darkstone aka LetsGlitchIt, Nickelly Garbaje, Professor Wrecks, Cyshimi, Xelda Jara, Glitch of Mind, Tyler Givens, and Laurel Charleston. Each artist has received a 1 ETH grant award for their artistic excellence and commitment to the culture. Each artist will be releasing an NFT edition here on [Zora.co](http://zora.co/).

The mission of QMoDA, The Queer Museum of Digital Art, is to create a supportive environment in the web3 space for Trans and Queer artists to thrive. We do this by collecting and preserving art on-chain, supporting artists financially, and looking for expansive ways to preserve cultural contributions by Trans and Queer creators globally. Learn more at Qmoda.art

Kate the Cursed Bio: I was born on the eve of y2k (the world did not end). I had a lonely childhood that smelled like cigarettes and dusty CRT TVs. When I was 4, I was told to be a man and had my Barbie dolls smashed. Little did they know, I’d grow up to be a doll myself. I developed insomnia and started watching 80s sci-fi movies on VHS over and over all night. As soon as I turned 18 I started taking female hormones and making art to process the new feels. At 20, I dropped out of film school to pursue an independent glitch art career and was posting my work as Kate the Cursed. The rest is history. <3

These are the words I want to say when I float away and leave my body behind. 

Time dissipates when I am dancing. My movement encapsulates the interconnectedness of memory, instinct, emotion, and truth. But when the sweat dries and the clocks start up again, my identity can become distorted and blurred. Regret, guilt, fear, and loss flood my mind, ripping me away from the love that colors my life.

This is disassociating for me; I am no longer in control of my body, words, or feelings and I am a shell with empty eyes. My mind hovers and every conversation is empty. My loved ones feel abandoned while we are sitting right across from one another. I wrote these lyrics while fighting a dissociative episode and I managed to come back to myself through making my experience tangible and real with words and sound.

This song is a reclamation of myself. When I’m ready to become real again, patient love is always there to welcome me back home.

“Fragmentación” (2019) is a video art piece by Ecuadorian multidisciplinary artist Doménica García. 

“Fragmentación” takes place in a magical realist Mexico City where two women embark on a journey through their sexuality. “Fragmentación” is a continuous compilation of 10 video art pieces that merge elements of performance art and traditional cinema. Each scene is a forgotten memory, portrayed by a visual metaphor with a unique surrealist touch. "Fragmentación" was produced in conjunction with the Ministry of Culture of Mexico City.

“Fragmentación: Papaya” is García’s first piece minted on the Ethereum Blockchain. The artist will release the remaining 9 video art pieces that make up the full film “Fragmentación” to acquire for collection.

Fragmentación has been screened and exhibited at the Museum of the Moving Image, Queens, NY; Bushwick Film Festival, Brooklyn, NY; Microscope Gallery, New York, NY; Granoff Center for the Creative Arts at Brown University, Providence, RI.

About the Artist
 
Doménica García (b. 1996, Quito, Ecuador) is an Ecuadorian multidisciplinary artist based in New York. Her work delves into a process of introspection, exploring the personal and discovering the universal. With the use of a hyperbolic language and the juxtaposition of the radical with the ordinary, she gives greater relevance to the day-to-day experience. García’s multimedia approach, particularly merging performance and digital art, allows her to manipulate the perception of reality, facilitating a fantastic and surreal experience within the rational world. 

García’s work has been shown in the Atlanta Film Festival, Atlanta, GA; San Diego Latino Film Festival, San Diego, CA; Queens Museum, Queens, NY; Museum of the Moving Image, Queens, NY; Institute of Contemporary Art Boston, Boston, MA; Centro de Arte Contemporáneo de Quito, Quito, EC; Microscope Gallery, New York, NY; Center for Performance Research, Brooklyn, NY; and Granoff Center for the Creative Arts, Providence, RI. 

García is a recipient of the New York Foundation For The Arts (NYFA) NFT Award, Foundation for Contemporary Arts (FCA) Emergency Grant, Studio Relief Residency at NARS Foundation, Center of Performance Research (CPR) Artist in Residence, Smack Mellon Artist in Residence, New York Community Trust Van Lier Fellowship.

García earned a BFA from the School of Visual Arts and is currently pursuing an MFA at Columbia University.

Hello ! Forrest here. You have come to this "ticket stub" because you've just finished your museum experience, or because you found this NFT via another avenue. Either way, welcome, and thanks for being here. I'd like to take this opportunity to reflect on how I myself, have come to this moment, and what this ticket stub means to me :3

So - the Museum of Forrest is an online gallery of 4 exhibits I self-curated to reflect my own lived stories, and the processes surrounding my diverse creative outputs. [www.museumofforrest.com] It came about when, after running with CY's idea to mint my artistic process NFTs weekly, we realized there wasn't a vibey place for all of these artifacts to live, let alone for their overarching story to be told. So, along with the massive help of Ana Wang, we created this museum-before-NFT-giftshop. As far as we know, it is the first of its kind.

While not all 900+ datapoints that I found demarcating my entire and ever-expanding body of work could be included in the museum itself, we did create a categorized database to hold them all in, which is also available for your viewing pleasure. [bit.ly/archivesofforrest] We then whittled down that list into 65 mindfully curated pieces, including songs, meditations, essays, music videos, and even photos of me on stage as a kid. These are the artifacts that now make up the Museum of Forrest.

The act of reflecting upon my whole lifetime's worth of self-expression from this retrospective vantage point has been absolutely remarkable. This project arrived at an already pivotal stage in my journey, where I've just hit 30, just moved back to my hometown, and just (mere days ago) applied for my legal name and gender change. I see myself clearer than ever, and have a greater sense of confidence and self-agency than I ever knew I would get to embody.

I am proud of myself. I am proud of what I've come through. I am proud of the man I have grown up to become. And while the majority of the work documented in this museum was born under a previous name, I know that every experience leading up to this moment was an invaluable stepping-stone, paving the path for the person I get to show up as today. Here and now, I can finally see Forrest through the trees. Thank you for seeing him with me.

[www.museumofforrest.com]
[bit.ly/archivesofforrest]

Limited edition (50) featuring a truncated narrative and unique sonification elements not included in the open edition of the piece.

Oil and water do not mix. Our biosphere and bodies require water; the Anthropocene as we know it continues to thirst for oil. Can the accelerating breakdown of global climate systems be understood through the lens of this elemental incompatibility?

Constructed with custom sonification tools developed by Pred in Max/MSP, nearly all musical components of the piece are generated from data sets exploring the impact of petroleum on our waterways and ice caps, access to drinking water, hydropower usage, and the price of crude oil.

The goal is not to translate these data points in a literal way, but to use them as starting points for creative exploration. If data is the new oil, can it fuel creativity - not just capture profit? Aside from the biases so often inherent in its collection, data tends to be corrupted in its expression, collapsing reality into abstraction. Composing with arbitrary musical outputs generated from these data sets reflects the dubious nature of much contemporary data usage.

Visualized by the artist in TouchDesigner, freely available drone footage of oil fields and processing facilities are contrasted with aquatic elements, manipulated and depicted in the bounds of a truncated circle, overlaid with pixelated data trails implying the degrading effect of digitized information itself. 


Total length: 2:34

Credits:
Audio + Visuals: Noah Pred
Publicly available datasets used for the audio were obtained from:
https://ourworldindata.org/
https://data.noaa.gov/datasetsearch/
https://finance.yahoo.com/
Drone footage used for the visuals obtained from: https://www.pexels.com/ 

Technical details: All sound design, production, and visual outputs by Noah Pred. Created using Max/MSP, Ableton Live, and TouchDesigner. 1080p MP4.

Life Without Water is one of the first songs Kena Rose wrote entirely on her own. She brought it to her dad, Genzo, and the production and recording was done within a couple hours. The next day, Kena said, “let’s go shoot a video!” Despite Genzo’s protests about the cold, rainy weather, the lateness in the day, and the high probability of hitting rush hour traffic, the two headed out, armed with a small setup to film, and by midnight that night the video was complete. The combination of Jimmery Caine’s cynicism and razor-sharp delivery, with Victor’s nosebleed-inducing bass and beats, has created music like nothing heard before.

Description:
I created this Music NFT as a reminder of sunny days, of childhood, of carelessness and lightness. Do you remember those days when you were so free and happy and you didn’t have any problems? I want you to stay in this lightness of mind all the time. Just listen to my song, look at the footage. I hope that I was able to convey to you the atmosphere of those times of freeness.

Difficult times and problems  will always happen in our lives, I understand this perfectly. But, there are also good moments in our life. Just take a closer look around. So let's focus on the positive aspects. 

To everyone who viewed this video, to everyone who heard this song - I wish you to be happy!
